about.title: Orland Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Orland's economy runs on a mix of agriculture, trucking, and small local businesses, and that mix brings its own set of workplace hazards — heavy machinery, forklifts, delivery vehicles, and roadwork near corridors like 6th Street and South Street. When a work injury happens, California generally routes the claim through workers' compensation, which pays medical costs and wage replacement regardless of fault, but doesn't cover pain and suffering. If someone outside your employer — a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver — contributed to the accident, you may also have grounds for a separate third-party injury claim. That second path can matter for someone in Orland driving for work along Rt 32 or handling equipment on a job site off Walker Street. LawProactive doesn't practice law or guarantee any result; we simply connect injured workers with an independent attorney who can look at both the comp claim and any possible third-party case, at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Orland Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: We Understand the Exclusive Remedy Rule
items.desc: California generally limits your claim against an employer to workers' compensation, but that doesn't close the door on every option. An attorney can review whether a third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — also bears responsibility.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California law expects a workplace injury to be reported to your employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate your comp claim. We help connect you quickly so an attorney can advise on next steps before time runs out.

items.title: Retaliation Protections Exist
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If you're worried about your job, an independent attorney can explain your protections under California law.

items.question: I was hurt while driving for work near Rt 32 — is that just a workers' comp claim?
items.answer: It could be more than that. If another driver caused the crash while you were on the job, you may have both a workers' comp claim through your employer and a separate third-party injury claim against the at-fault driver. An independent attorney can sort out which claims apply and how the two-year deadline for third-party claims fits your situation.

items.question: What if my employer in Orland doesn't want me to report the injury?
items.answer: Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury is illegal in California, regardless of employer size or industry. You generally have 30 days to report the injury to preserve your workers' comp rights, so it's best not to delay even if you feel pressure not to say anything.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. We don't guarantee any outcome, but we can help you get a conversation started quickly.
